title: Leukocyte SUbtype measurements with Raman SPECTroscopy of Healthy Donors' blood samples
summary:
This observational study investigates whether different types of white blood cells can be reliably distinguished using a special light-based measurement technique. The aim is to establish a reference database of measurements obtained from healthy adults. This database will provide a basis for the development and validation of new methods for blood sample analysis.
Healthy adults will participate in the study. Blood samples will be collected at five predefined time points over a period of one year. No treatment or changes to the participants' medical care will take place. Different types of white blood cells will be examined, and their measurement data will be compared. The study will also assess how much the measurements vary between different individuals and within the same individual over time. In addition, it will investigate whether the measurement data change when prepared blood samples are stored for several days. The results will be compared with those obtained from a standard laboratory blood cell analysis.

interventions.name: In this observational study, healthy adult participants will have blood samples collected five times over a one-year observation period for the spectroscopic characterization of leukocytes. A complete blood count and the HiL index (hemolysis, icterus, and lipemia index) will be recorded as reference

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-    Free of infections or fever for the past two weeks
-    Written consent form
Exclusion criteria:
-    chronic conditions (e.g., cancer, anemia, HIV infection, hepatitis, intestinal worms, and other parasites in the blood, etc.)
-    pregnancy or breastfeeding
-    blood transfusion
-    acute infection, fever, or elevated inflammatory markers (CRP)
